title: A spinning skater pulls in her arms
hook: A skater spins slowly with arms out, then pulls them in. How much faster does she turn?

knows: skaters spin faster when they pull their arms in
turns per second as a spin rate
doesNotKnow: moment of inertia: how spread out mass is around the spin axis
that angular momentum, moment of inertia times spin rate, stays fixed when nothing outside twists the spinner

misconception: Pulling the arms in squeezes out a bit more spin, by some unspecified amount.
objective: The learner can explain that with no outside twist, moment of inertia times spin rate stays the same, so cutting the moment of inertia to a third triples the spin rate.

claims.text: Moment of inertia (I, in kg·m²) measures how far a body's mass sits from its spin axis: each bit of mass counts times its distance squared.
claims.source: I = sum of m r^2. OpenStax University Physics Vol. 1, section 10.4 Moment of Inertia and Rotational Kinetic Energy.

claims.text: With no outside twist (torque), angular momentum, I times spin rate, stays the same.
claims.source: Conservation of angular momentum, L = I omega: OpenStax University Physics Vol. 1, section 11.3 Conservation of Angular Momentum (uses the spinning skater as its example).

claims.text: Starting at 1 turn per second with I = 3.0 kg·m², she spins 1.5 turns per second at I = 2.0 and 3 turns per second at I = 1.0; I × spin stays 3.0.
claims.source: omega2 = I1 omega1 / I2: 3.0 x 1 / 2.0 = 1.5; 3.0 x 1 / 1.0 = 3.0 turns per second (node; spin() in Demo.tsx).

claims.text: The moments of inertia (3.0 kg·m² with arms out, 1.0 tucked) are illustrative values for a skater, and the arm lengths on the stage are drawn to suggest them, not to scale.
claims.source: Builder's illustrative values, from the brief; measured figures for spinning skaters are of this order (arms out a few kg·m², tucked about 1). Labelled 'illustrative' on stage.

claims.text: Idealisation: frictionless ice and no air drag, so nothing outside twists her.
claims.source: Stated on stage. Real skates and air slow a spin a little over many turns.

recall.question: A diver tucks tightly in mid-air, halving her moment of inertia. Her spin rate...
recall.why: In the air nothing outside twists her, so moment of inertia times spin rate stays fixed: half the moment of inertia means twice the spin.
